A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of prior knowledge about the genomic regions that contain informative SNPs, the ascertainment algorithm we developed is a valuable tool for selecting the most informative markers for the identification of population structure and genetic ancestries.
we have identified a set of 10 SNPs, which are informative for the detection of continental population structure and which are likely to have evolved under positive selection.

the ascertainment procedure we developed can be used for the efficient identification of genetic ancestry and population structure, even when the genetic diversity is distributed continuously across a wide geographic range, such as that of human populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with the help of our newly developed ascertainment method, it is possible to identify genetic ancestry on the continental level with only 10 SNPs.

the ascertainment of a minimal set (i.e. only 10) of SNPs for the identification of genetic ancestry is feasible and that the genomic regions surrounding these SNPs are under local positive selection.
, by using the appropriate ascertainment algorithm, a small number of carefully selected SNPs is able to capture the major features of global population structure.
